card.thesis: Holds three sleeves: QQQ (55%, the Nasdaq-100 core -- unleveraged, no 2x fund anywhere in this card, deliberately, for the identical 'leverage trap' reason ALLOCATION-FAMILY.md gives for its own four variants), IEF (25%, 7-10yr Treasuries, the duration ballast), GLD (20%, gold, the sleeve least correlated with either QQQ or IEF). QQQ carries the largest single weight in this round's entire candidate field specifically because this card is purpose=trading -- a $100,000 lump sum with no horizon constraint and no contribution stream to average into a chosen entry price (PurposeSpec.horizon_years_max is None for TRADING, per the owner's own 2026-08-24 correction) -- which is the one purpose in this round where a concentrated bet on the single highest-CAGR simple index this programme has measured is not diluted or protected by dollar-cost-averaging the way the savings and Roth arms' monthly/annual drips would blunt it. QQQ, not SPY, is the core for exactly the reason round 15's own prediction 4 states: 'no candidate will beat QQQ buy-and-hold on raw return' has been true of every diversified, unlevered variant ALLOCATION-FAMILY.md tested against a SPY core; this card tests whether replacing the core itself, rather than diversifying around SPY, closes some of that gap, at the cost of the concentration risk a genuinely whole-market core would not carry. What makes it move: one rule, evaluated against QQQ's own bars only (no cross-symbol operator exists in this engine) -- when QQQ's own rolling ATR(14) exceeds 2.8% of its own close (QQQ's own historical ATR/close ratio, measured directly off the stored bar series: median approximately 1.61%, 75th percentile approximately 2.44%, so 2.8% sits just above the 80th percentile -- the same 'read the threshold off the instrument's own distribution' discipline ALLOCATION-FAMILY.md used for SPY's 1.8% and ROTH-VOLTARGET.md used for QLD, not a round number), shift 10 points of the book from QQQ into IEF. The card is stateless: because AllocationCard rebuilds every session's target weights fresh from the declared base plus whichever rules fire that same session, the tilt reverts to the 55/25/20 base automatically the session ATR falls back at or below 2.8%, with nothing carried over. This is betting that a spike in QQQ's own realised range is more often followed by continued or deepening weakness than by an immediate V-shaped recovery -- a defensive, not a momentum, read of elevated volatility. Falsification: this thesis is wrong, not merely unlucky, if QQQ's own ATR spikes are systematically followed by strength rather than further weakness or chop -- i.e. the rule sells a scare that was actually the entry point, giving back exactly the recovery a buy-and-hold QQQ position would have captured, which is precisely what ALLOCATION-FAMILY.md's own vol-target variant 3 showed happening at a 20% target (a higher-vol regime is often simply 'more QQQ, all the time' in disguise, and fighting that with a defensive tilt gives back the market's own best years along with its worst). It is also falsified if the single rule's turnover cost, in slippage, exceeds the drawdown reduction it buys -- the same test ALLOCATION-FAMILY.md applied to its own two-rule ATR tilt, which only barely passed (25bp of final balance for a 1.6-point drawdown improvement). Who is on the other side of the trade: when this card sells QQQ into IEF on an ATR spike, the buyer on the other side is someone reading the same spike as a buying opportunity in a growth-heavy index -- and across QQQ's own post-2004 history that buyer has more often than not been right, which is the honest cost of holding a defensive rule against the single highest-returning core this programme has measured. Parameter count against the ten-parameter budget: 2 free sleeve weights (QQQ, IEF; GLD is determined by the sum-to-one constraint) plus 1 band_pct plus 2 rule parameters (the 0.028 ATR threshold, the 0.10 shift_pct) = 5 of 10. Expected window eligibility: bound by GLD's 2004-11-18 start (QQQ 1999-03-10, IEF 2002-07-30, GLD 2004-11-18 -- GLD is latest), well before every window in the round's main matrix and every long window (h10y-1/h10y-2/h5y-1/h5y-2/h5y-3 all begin 2013-09-03 or later); eligible across the full main-window matrix back to late 2004, and since this is a trading-purpose card it is scored on lump-sum median adjusted_excess over the main matrix, not gated by the three-long-window contribution rule that binds the savings and Roth arms.
